name: mesh-convergence
title: Mesh convergence: FEM rigor
question:
Does the `PoissonSolverStep` wrapper deliver the theoretical O(h^2) mesh
convergence rate for P1 Lagrange elements, or does the wrapping introduce
an artifact that masks/inflates the true discretization error?
hypothesis:
On a superconvergence-resistant (crossed-diagonal) unit-square mesh, the
L2 error of a P1 (degree=1) solve should scale as O(h^2) across a
resolution sweep, giving an observed log-log slope near 2.
objective:
Sweep the `mesh_convergence` composite's `resolution` parameter (8, 16, 32)
at fixed polynomial degree 1, fit the L2-error-vs-mesh-size slope on a
log-log plot, and confirm the fitted rate matches the theoretical
O(h^(degree+1)) convergence order.
description:
Reuses `PoissonSolverStep` (as `poisson-validation` does) but at
degree=1 and swept over `resolution`, via the `mesh_convergence` composite
generator -- one composite build per sweep point (the sweep itself lives
in this study's `variants:`/runner, not in the generator, which
parameterizes a single (resolution, degree) pair). `fem.build_mesh` uses
dolfinx's "crossed" triangulation specifically to avoid a known P1
superconvergence artifact on the default "right" diagonal that would
collapse the error to round-off at every resolution and mask the true
rate.

expected_behavior.name: convergence-rate-matches-order
expected_behavior.en: The fitted log-log convergence rate across resolution=[8,16,32] is at least 1.7 (theoretical O(h^2) is 2.0).
expected_behavior.rationale: P1 Lagrange elements on a non-superconvergent mesh should converge at the theoretical O(h^2) rate for the L2 norm; a rate below 1.7 would indicate either a solver bug or an unintended superconvergence artifact (the same band tests/test_poisson.py::test_convergence_rate locks).

behavior_tests.name: convergence-rate-matches-order
behavior_tests.description:
The fitted slope of log(l2_error) vs log(h) across resolution=[8,16,32]
must be at or above 1.7 (theoretical O(h^2) is 2.0; 1.7 leaves headroom
for mesh-dependent noise while still ruling out a broken/first-order
solve).

provenance.note: Standard FEM a priori error theory gives O(h^(k+1)) for degree-k Lagrange elements in the L2 norm; k=1 implies rate=2. 1.7 is a calibration margin below the theoretical value, not a fitted threshold.

embed_visualizations.name: convergence-loglog
embed_visualizations.description: Interactive Plotly log-log convergence plot (L2 error vs mesh resolution).
